The node `root>low` creates a new stacking context because it is positioned and has a non-auto `z-index` (1). This means the `z-index: 999` of `root>low>inner` is scoped entirely within `root>low` and cannot lift it above elements in a higher stacking context. Since `root>high` has a `z-index` of 2, it paints on top of the entire `root>low` stacking context and its descendants.

ANSWER: root>high
